name: Footer
description: The page footer: a copyright line and secondary links such as Privacy, Terms and Help. It is the page’s content-info landmark.
whenToUse: Once per page, at the bottom, for legal text and secondary links.

whenNotToUse.text: For the main sections of the site.
For the end of an article or card.

anatomy.name: Links
anatomy.description: A labelled navigation list of secondary links.

values.meaning: A button that runs onClick, e.g. “Cookie settings”.

behavior.text: Links wrap onto more rows on narrow screens.
A top-level footer is the contentinfo landmark; its links are a nav named by linksLabel (default “Footer”).

content: Text: “© 2026 Company”. Use the current year from code, not a hard-coded one.

guidelines.dont: Use buttons that change location in JavaScript.
guidelines.why: Links can be opened in new tabs and are announced as links.

guidelines.dont: Repeat the whole Navbar in the footer.
guidelines.why: Duplicate navigation adds noise for keyboard and screen reader users.
Several contentinfo landmarks confuse landmark navigation.

accessibility.role: contentinfo landmark (footer) with a named navigation list.
accessibility.focus: Each link shows the focus ring.

wcag.how: Text and links pass 4.5:1 in every theme.

examples.title: Footer
With an in-page action
examples.description: A link without href becomes a button.

related.relation: The main navigation at the top.

changes: Links are real links (href) in a labelled nav list; items without href are buttons.
Own --footer-* tokens instead of button and section tokens; hover underlines instead of a raw-color background.
